tldr: TxAgent is an AI agent that integrates multi-step reasoning with real-time retrieval from a toolbox of 211 biomedical tools, outperforming leading large language models on drug reasoning and personalized treatment benchmarks.
contributions: Introduction of TxAgent, an AI agent for therapeutic reasoning with transparent multi-step reasoning traces.
Development of TOOLUNIVERSE, a biomedical toolbox consolidating 211 expert-curated tools from trusted sources (openFDA, Open Targets, Monarch Initiative).
Creation of TOOLRAG, an adaptive tool retrieval model, and TOOLGEN, a multi-agent system for generating tools from API documentation.
Construction of TXAGENT-INSTRUCT dataset with 378,027 instruction-tuning samples derived from 85,340 multi-step reasoning traces.
Introduction of five new benchmarks (DrugPC, BrandPC, GenericPC, DescriptionPC, TreatmentPC) for evaluating drug reasoning and personalized treatment.
methods: TxAgent is built by fine-tuning the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on TXAGENT-INSTRUCT, a dataset generated by agent systems (QUESTIONGEN, TRACEGEN, TOOLGEN) that produce therapeutic questions, reasoning traces, and tool specifications. The agent leverages TOOLUNIVERSE, a suite of 211 tools covering adverse events, pharmacology, clinical guidelines, and disease annotations, with TOOLRAG dynamically selecting relevant tools based on query context. It performs iterative multi-step reasoning, executing function calls to retrieve real-time biomedical knowledge from verified sources, and synthesizes answers with transparent reasoning traces. Performance is evaluated on five newly constructed benchmarks spanning drug reasoning tasks and personalized treatment scenarios.
results: TxAgent achieves 92.1% accuracy on the DrugPC open-ended drug reasoning benchmark, surpassing GPT-4o by 25.8% and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct by 39.3%. It maintains an accuracy variance of <0.01 across brand, generic, and description-based drug references, whereas GPT-4o exhibits a variance of 9.96. On DescriptionPC, TxAgent attains 56.5% accuracy, outperforming GPT-4o by 8.3%. In personalized treatment (TreatmentPC), it outperforms GPT-4o by 13.6% and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct by 25.4%. Additionally, TxAgent achieves 7.5% higher accuracy than DeepSeek-R1 (671B) in open-ended queries.
limitations: The paper does not explicitly detail limitations, but evident constraints include dependence on the coverage and real-time availability of external biomedical tools and APIs. The approach may be limited to drugs and conditions represented in the source databases (FDA-approved drugs since 1939, Open Targets). Hallucination detection is performed during dataset generation, but the paper does not report systematic hallucination rates in TxAgent's outputs. Computational overhead from multi-step reasoning and tool execution is not quantified.
